sentences.zh: 劉彥宗

translations.literal: Liu Yanzong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzong

sentences.zh: 劉彥宗，子魯開，大興宛平人。

translations.literal: Liu Yanzong, courtesy name Lukai, was a native of Wanping in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzong, whose courtesy name was Lukai, came from Wanping in Daxing.

sentences.zh: 遠祖怦，唐盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: His distant ancestor Zheng was military governor of Lulong under the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His distant ancestor Zheng had served the Tang as military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 石晉以幽、薊入遼，劉氏六世仕遼，相繼為宰相。

translations.literal: When the Later Jin ceded You and Ji to Liao, the Liu clan served Liao for six generations, successive chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: After the Later Jin ceded You and Ji to Liao, the Liu family served Liao for six generations in succession as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 父霄，至中京留守。

translations.literal: His father Xiao rose to be defender of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao rose to become defender of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 彥宗擢進士乙科。

translations.literal: Yanzong was selected in the second rank of the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong passed the jinshi examination in the second rank.

sentences.zh: 天祚走天德，秦晉國王耶律捏裏自立于燕，擢彥宗留守判官。

translations.literal: When Tianzuo fled to Tiande, the Prince of Qin and Jin, Yelü Nieli, established himself in Yan and promoted Yanzong to deputy defender.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tianzuo fled to Tiande, Yelü Nieli, Prince of Qin and Jin, declared himself in Yan and appointed Yanzong deputy defender.

sentences.zh: 蕭妃攝政，遷簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiao acted as regent, he was transferred to deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the regency of Empress Xiao, he was promoted to deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖至居庸關，蕭妃自古北口遁去，都監高六送款于太祖。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor reached Juyong Pass, Empress Xiao fled through the Northern Pass, and the metropolitan supervisor Gao Liu offered his allegiance to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor reached Juyong Pass, Empress Xiao fled through the Northern Pass while the metropolitan supervisor Gao Liu submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 太祖奄至，駐蹕城南，彥宗與左企弓等奉表降。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor arrived suddenly, halted south of the city, and Yanzong with Zuo Qigong and others presented a memorial of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor arrived unexpectedly and halted south of the city; Yanzong, Zuo Qigong, and others presented a memorial of surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖一見，器遇之，俾復舊，遷左僕射，佩金牌。

translations.literal: At their first meeting the Grand Ancestor valued him highly, restored his former status, promoted him to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and bestowed a gold tablet.
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting the Grand Ancestor took a strong liking to him, restored his former standing, appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and awarded him a gold tablet.

sentences.zh: 張覺為南京留守，太祖聞覺有異志，使彥宗、斜缽宣慰之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue was defender of the Southern Capital; hearing that Jue harbored disloyal intent, the Grand Ancestor sent Yanzong and Xiebo to console and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue was defender of the Southern Capital. When the Grand Ancestor heard that Jue harbored disloyal intent, he sent Yanzong and Xiebo to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 太祖至鴛鴦濼，不豫，還上京，留宗翰都統軍事，留彥宗佐之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor reached Yuanyang Marsh, fell ill, and returned to the Upper Capital, leaving Zonghan as overall military commander and Yanzong to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor reached Yuanyang Marsh, fell ill, and returned to the Upper Capital, leaving Zonghan in overall command of the armies with Yanzong to assist him.

sentences.zh: 及張覺敗奔于宋，眾推張敦固為都統，殺使者，乘城拒守，攻之不肯下。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jue was defeated and fled to Song, the crowd made Zhang Dungu commander-in-chief; they killed the envoy, manned the walls in defense, and would not yield though attacked.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jue was defeated and fled to Song, the troops installed Zhang Dungu as commander-in-chief, killed the envoy, held the walls, and refused to surrender despite repeated assaults.

sentences.zh: 彥宗同中書門下平章事，知樞密院事，加侍中，佐宗望軍。

translations.literal: Yanzong was made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and additionally Palace Attendant, assisting Zongwang's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong was appointed Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with the additional title of Palace Attendant, to assist Zongwang's army.

sentences.zh: 宗望奏，方圖攻取，凡州縣之事委彥宗裁決之。

translations.literal: Zongwang memorialized that he was still planning the assault and entrusted all prefectural and county affairs to Yanzong's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang reported that he was still planning the assault and entrusted all prefectural and county affairs to Yanzong's judgment.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，詔彥宗曰：「中京等兩路先多拒命，故遣使撫諭，貰其官民之罪，所犯在降附前者勿論。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui an edict to Yanzong said: "The two circuits of the Central Capital and elsewhere first largely refused orders; therefore envoys are sent to console and instruct, pardoning the offenses of officials and people—crimes committed before submission are not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhui an edict told Yanzong: "The two circuits centered on the Central Capital had largely refused our orders, so we are sending envoys to reassure them and pardon the offenses of officials and commoners. Crimes committed before they submitted are not to be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 卿等選官與使者往諭之，使勤於稼穡。

translations.literal: You and others are to select officials to go with the envoys to instruct them and urge diligence in farming."
translations.idiomatic: Select officials to accompany the envoys and instruct the people to devote themselves to agriculture."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，大舉伐宋，彥宗畫十策，詔彥宗兼領漢軍都統。

translations.literal: Not long after, a major campaign was launched against Song; Yanzong drafted ten strategies, and an edict appointed him also overall commander of the Han armies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a major campaign was launched against Song. Yanzong drafted ten strategies, and an edict named him overall commander of the Han armies as well.

sentences.zh: 蔡靖以燕山降。

translations.literal: Cai Jing surrendered Yan Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing surrendered the Yan Mountains region.

sentences.zh: 詔彥宗凡燕京一品以下官皆承制注授，遂進兵伐宋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Yanzong confer all offices in Yanjing from first rank down by imperial commission, and the army then advanced against Song.
translations.idiomatic: An edict empowered Yanzong to appoint all officials in Yanjing from first rank downward, after which the army advanced against Song.

sentences.zh: 至汴，宋少帝割地納質，師還。

translations.literal: Reaching Bian, the young Song emperor ceded territory and sent hostages, and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Bian, the young Song emperor ceded territory and sent hostages, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宗望分將士屯安肅、雄、霸、廣信之境，留闍母、彥宗于燕京節制諸軍。

translations.literal: Zongwang distributed officers and soldiers to garrison Ansu, Xiong, Ba, and Guangxin, leaving She Mu and Yanzong at Yanjing to command the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang distributed troops to garrison Ansu, Xiong, Ba, and Guangxin, while She Mu and Yanzong remained at Yanjing to command the armies.

sentences.zh: 明年，再伐宋，已圍汴京，彥宗謂宗翰、宗望曰：「蕭何入關，秋毫無犯，惟收圖籍。

translations.literal: The next year they campaigned against Song again; already besieging Bianjing, Yanzong told Zonghan and Zongwang: "When Xiao He entered the passes he took not a hair in spoil, only collecting registers and maps.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they campaigned against Song again. With Bianjing already besieged, Yanzong told Zonghan and Zongwang: "When Xiao He entered the passes he took not a hair in spoil, only collecting registers and maps.

sentences.zh: 遼太宗入汴，載路車、法服、石經以歸，皆令則也。

translations.literal: When the Liao Taizong entered Bian he carried off the imperial carriage, ritual robes, and stone classics—all models to follow."
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao Taizong entered Bian he carried off the imperial carriage, ritual vestments, and stone classics—all precedents worth following."

sentences.zh: 」二帥嘉納之，執二帝以歸。

translations.literal: The two commanders praised and accepted this, seized the two emperors, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Both commanders approved the advice, took the two Song emperors captive, and returned.

sentences.zh: 天會六年薨，年五十三，追封鄆王。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Tianhui, aged fifty-three, and was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Tianhui at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，例降封開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, by precedent his title was reduced to Grand Preceptor with the privilege of an opening office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong his posthumous rank was reduced by precedent to Grand Preceptor with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，追封兗國公，諡英敏。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading he was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Yan State with the posthumous name Yingmin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Dading he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yan with the posthumous name Yingmin.

sentences.zh: 子萼、筈。

translations.literal: His sons were E and Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were E and Kuo.

sentences.zh: 子 萼

translations.literal: Son E
translations.idiomatic: Son E

sentences.zh: 萼，彥宗季子也。

translations.literal: E was Yanzong's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: E was Yanzong's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 遼末以廕補閣門祗候。

translations.literal: At the end of Liao he entered office by hereditary privilege as usher of the Inner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Liao he entered office by hereditary privilege as usher of the Inner Gate.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年，授禮賓使，累官德州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu he was appointed commissioner of ritual guests and rose through offices to military commissioner of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianfu he was appointed commissioner of ritual guests and eventually rose to military commissioner of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 天德初，稍加擢用，曆左右宣徽使，拜參知政事，進尚書左丞，為沁南軍節度使，曆臨洮、太原尹。

translations.literal: Early in Tiande he was gradually promoted, served as Left and Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed Vice Grand Councilor, advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, became military commissioner of the Qinnan Army, and served as prefect of Lintao and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiande era he was gradually promoted, serving as Left and Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, Vice Grand Councilor, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then military commissioner of the Qinnan Army and prefect of Lintao and Taiyuan in turn.

sentences.zh: 正隆南伐，為漢南道行營兵馬都統制。

translations.literal: During the southern campaign of Zhenglong he was overall commander of the mobile camp armies of the Hannan Route.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign of Zhenglong he served as overall commander of the mobile camp armies on the Hannan Route.

sentences.zh: 大定初，除興中尹，封任國公，曆順天、定武軍節度使、濟南尹。

translations.literal: Early in Dading he was made prefect of Xingzhong, enfeoffed Duke of Ren State, and served as military commissioner of Shuntian and Dingwu armies and prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he was appointed prefect of Xingzhong and enfeoffed as Duke of Ren, then served as military commissioner of Shuntian and Dingwu and as prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 萼淫縱無行，所至貪墨狼籍。

translations.literal: E was licentious and unrestrained in conduct; wherever he went his corruption was notorious.
translations.idiomatic: E was dissolute and unrestrained, and wherever he served his corruption was notorious.

sentences.zh: 廉使劾之，詔遣大理少卿張九思就濟南鞫問。

translations.literal: The integrity commissioner impeached him, and an edict sent Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Jiusi to Jinan to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: An integrity commissioner impeached him, and an edict sent Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Jiusi to Jinan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 既就逮，不測所以，引刃自殺，不死。

translations.literal: Once arrested and not knowing what would befall him, he drew a blade to kill himself but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Once arrested and uncertain of his fate, he tried to kill himself with a blade but survived.

sentences.zh: 詔削官一階，罷歸田裏，卒。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of one rank, dismissed him to his home district, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of one rank, sent him home to his district, and he died there.

sentences.zh: 子仲詢，天德三年，賜王彥潛榜及第。

translations.literal: His son Zhongxun, in the third year of Tiande, was granted graduation on the list of Wang Yanqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongxun graduated on the examination list of Wang Yanqian in the third year of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 子 筈

translations.literal: Son Kuo
translations.idiomatic: Son Kuo

sentences.zh: 筈，彥宗次子。

translations.literal: Kuo was Yanzong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was Yanzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 幼時以廕隸閣門，不就，去從學。

translations.literal: In youth he was enrolled in the Inner Gate by privilege but did not take the post and left to pursue study.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was enrolled in the Inner Gate by hereditary privilege but declined the post and left to study.

sentences.zh: 遼末調兵，而筈在選中。

translations.literal: At the end of Liao troops were levied, and Kuo was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Liao, when troops were levied, Kuo was among those selected.

sentences.zh: 遼兵敗，左右多散亡，乃選筈為扈從，授左承制。

translations.literal: When Liao forces were defeated many attendants scattered; he was then chosen as an escort attendant and appointed Left Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao forces were defeated and many attendants scattered, he was chosen as an escort attendant and appointed Left Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遼主西奔，蕭妃攝政，賜筈進士第，授尚書左司員外郎，寄班閣門。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler fled west; Empress Xiao acted as regent, granted Kuo the jinshi degree, appointed him Outer Vice Director of the Left Office of the Department of State Affairs, and attached him to the Inner Gate roster.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao ruler fled west, Empress Xiao acted as regent, granted Kuo the jinshi degree, appointed him Outer Vice Director of the Left Office of the Department of State Affairs, and attached him to the Inner Gate roster.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年，太祖取燕，筈從其父兄出降，遷尚書左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu, when the Grand Ancestor took Yan, Kuo followed his father and elder brothers in surrender and was transferred to Director of the Left Office of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianfu, when the Grand Ancestor took Yan, Kuo followed his father and elder brothers in surrendering and was appointed Director of the Left Office of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，授殿中少監。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，宋，夏遣使吊慰，凡館見禮儀皆筈詳定。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, Song and Xia sent envoys of condolence; Kuo worked out all protocols for receiving them in the hostel.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Ancestor's death, Song and Xia sent condolence envoys, and Kuo worked out all protocols for receiving them.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉少卿，授西上閣門使，仍從事元帥府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, appointed usher of the Western Upper Inner Gate, and continued to serve the Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, appointed usher of the Western Upper Inner Gate, and continued to serve at the Marshal's Office.

sentences.zh: 元帥府以便宜從事，凡約束廢置及四方號令多從筈之畫焉。

translations.literal: The Marshal's Office acted at discretion; most regulations abolished or instituted and orders to the four quarters followed Kuo's plans.
translations.idiomatic: The Marshal's Office acted at its own discretion, and most regulations issued or abolished and orders sent to the four quarters followed Kuo's plans.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，遷太常少卿、東上閣門使，從宗翰伐宋，圍太原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and usher of the Eastern Upper Inner Gate, followed Zonghan against Song, and besieged Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhui he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and usher of the Eastern Upper Inner Gate, accompanied Zonghan against Song, and besieged Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉卿，權簽宣徽院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and acting deputy director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and acting deputy director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，授左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Left Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 秋，複南征，權中書省樞密院事。

translations.literal: In autumn he campaigned south again as acting director of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he campaigned south again as acting director of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，明年起複，直樞密院事加給事中。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; the next year he was recalled from mourning, made direct director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with the additional title of Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled from mourning the following year as direct director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with the additional title of Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 七年，為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十年，改彰信軍節度使，權簽中書省樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and acting deputy director of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and acting deputy director of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，改左宣徽使，熙宗幸燕，法駕儀仗筈討論者為多。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he was changed to Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; when Xizong visited Yan, Kuo contributed much to the discussion of imperial carriage regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan he was appointed Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat. When Xizong visited Yan, Kuo contributed greatly to planning the imperial carriage regalia.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，充江南封冊使，假中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he served as envoy to invest the ruler south of the Yangzi, with the provisional title of Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangtong he served as envoy to invest the ruler south of the Yangzi, holding the provisional title of Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既至臨安，而宋人榜其居曰「行宮」，筈曰：「未受命，而名行宮，非也。

translations.literal: On reaching Lin'an the Song had posted his lodging as "Traveling Palace"; Kuo said: "Before receiving the investiture, to call it a traveling palace is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Lin'an he found the Song had posted his lodging as "Traveling Palace." Kuo said: "Before you have received the investiture, to call it a traveling palace is improper.

sentences.zh: 」請去榜而後行禮。

translations.literal: He asked that the placard be removed before ceremonies were performed."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the placard be removed before the ceremonies could proceed."

sentences.zh: 宋人驚服其有識，欲厚賄說之，奉金珠三十余萬，而筈不之顧，皆歎曰：「大國有人焉。」

translations.literal: The Song were startled and admired his discernment; wishing to win him with lavish bribes they offered more than three hundred thousand in gold and pearls, but Kuo paid no heed, and all sighed: "The great state has its men."
translations.idiomatic: The Song were astonished by his discernment and tried to win him with lavish bribes, offering more than three hundred thousand in gold and pearls, but Kuo would not look at them. All exclaimed: "The great state truly has its men."

sentences.zh: 六年，為行台尚書右丞相，兼判左宣徽使事，留京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was Right Grand Councilor of the Branch Secretariat, concurrently adjudicating Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat affairs, and remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was Right Grand Councilor of the Branch Secretariat, concurrently overseeing the Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, and remained at the capital.

sentences.zh: 或請厘革河南官吏之濫雜者，筈曰：「廢齊用兵江表，求一切近效，其所用人不必皆以章程，故有不由科目而為大吏，不試弓馬而握兵柄者。

translations.literal: Some asked to reform the mixed abuses among officials south of the river; Kuo said: "When Qi was abolished and troops were used on the Jiang table, immediate results were sought; those employed need not all follow regulations—hence some became high officials without examination ranks, and some held military authority without archery and horsemanship tests.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed reforming the confused mix of officials south of the river. Kuo said: "When Qi was abolished and troops were sent to the Jiang region, the court sought quick results. Those employed did not all follow regular procedures, so some became high officials without examination credentials and some held military command without archery and horsemanship tests.

sentences.zh: 今撫定未久，姑收人心，奈何為是紛更也。

translations.literal: Pacification is not long established; for now win hearts—why make such disruptive changes.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification is still recent. For now we should win hearts. Why stir up such disruptive changes.

sentences.zh: 」遂仍其舊。

translations.literal: The former arrangements were therefore kept.
translations.idiomatic: The former arrangements were therefore left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 七年，帥府議于館陶築三城，以為有警即令北軍入居之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Marshal's Office proposed building three cities at Guantao so that in an emergency northern troops could enter and dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Marshal's Office proposed building three cities at Guantao so that in an emergency northern troops could move in and occupy them.

sentences.zh: 筈曰：「今天下一家，孰為南北。

translations.literal: Kuo said: "Now all under Heaven is one family—who is north and who south.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo said: "All under Heaven is now one family. Who is north and who south.

sentences.zh: 設或有變，軍人入城，獨能安耶。

translations.literal: If there should be trouble, could soldiers entering the cities alone be secure?
translations.idiomatic: If trouble should arise, would soldiers entering the cities alone be any safer?

sentences.zh: 當嚴武備以察奸，無示彼此之間也。

translations.literal: We should tighten military readiness to detect treachery and not display a divide between us and them."
translations.idiomatic: We should tighten military readiness to detect treachery and not display a divide between us and them."

sentences.zh: 」其後，竟從筈議。

translations.literal: Afterward they ultimately followed Kuo's view.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they followed Kuo's advice.

sentences.zh: 初，以河外三州賜夏人，或言秦之在夏者數千人，皆願來歸。

translations.literal: Earlier the three prefectures beyond the river had been granted to the Xia; some said several thousand Qin people in Xia all wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the three prefectures beyond the river had been granted to Xia. Some reported that several thousand Qin people living in Xia wished to return.

sentences.zh: 諸將請約之，筈曰：「三小州不足為輕重，恐失朝廷大信。

translations.literal: The generals asked to arrange their return; Kuo said: "Three small prefectures are not worth the weight, and we may lose the court's great trust.
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked to arrange their return. Kuo said: "Three small prefectures are not worth the trouble, and we may lose the court's credibility.

sentences.zh: 且秦人之在蜀者倍多於此，何獨舍彼而取此乎。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin people in Shu are more than twice as many—why abandon those and take these?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Qin people in Shu are more than twice as numerous. Why abandon those and take these?

sentences.zh: 」遂從筈議。

translations.literal: They therefore followed Kuo's view.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore followed Kuo's advice.

sentences.zh: 陝西邊帥請完沿邊城郭以備南寇，筈曰：「我利車騎而不利城守。

translations.literal: The border commander of Shaanxi asked to complete frontier walls and cities against southern raiders; Kuo said: "We profit from chariots and cavalry, not from wall defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi frontier commander asked to complete the border fortifications against southern raids. Kuo said: "We profit from chariots and cavalry, not from holding walled cities.

sentences.zh: 今城之，則勞民而結怨。

translations.literal: If we fortify now, we weary the people and breed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Fortifying now would weary the people and breed resentment.

sentences.zh: 況盟已定，豈可妄動。

translations.literal: Moreover the alliance is settled—how can we act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the alliance is already settled. How can we act rashly.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷之。

translations.literal: The plan was therefore abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was therefore abandoned.

sentences.zh: 子 仲誨

translations.literal: Son Zhonghui
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhonghui

sentences.zh: 仲誨字子忠。

translations.literal: Zhonghui, courtesy name Zizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui, whose courtesy name was Zizhong.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，以宰相子授忠勇校尉。

translations.literal: Early in Huangtong, as a chancellor's son he was appointed Captain of Loyal Valor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong, as a chancellor's son he was appointed Captain of Loyal Valor.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜進士第，除應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was granted the jinshi degree and appointed literary attendant of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was granted the jinshi degree and appointed literary attendant of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 海陵嚴暴，臣下應對多失次。

translations.literal: Hailing was severe and violent; subordinates often lost composure in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was severe and violent, and officials often lost composure when answering him.

sentences.zh: 嘗以時政訪問在朝官，仲誨從容敷奏，無懼色，海陵稱賞之。

translations.literal: Once he questioned officials in court on current affairs; Zhonghui answered at ease without fear, and Hailing praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he questioned officials in court about current affairs. Zhonghui answered calmly without fear, and Hailing praised him.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，丁父憂，起複翰林修撰。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan he mourned his father, was recalled from mourning as Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, after mourning his father, he was recalled from mourning as Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，遷待制，尋兼修起居注、左補闕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was transferred to Attendant Drafting, soon also compiling the Veritable Records and serving as Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was promoted to Attendant Drafting, and soon also compiled the Veritable Records while serving as Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔仲誨與左司員外郎蒲察蒲速越廉問所過州縣，仲誨等還奏狀，詔玉田縣令李方進一階，順州知法、權密雲縣事王宗永擢密雲縣尉，順州司候張璘、密雲縣尉石抹烏者皆免去。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict ordered Zhonghui and Outer Vice Director of the Left Office Pucha Pusuyue to conduct integrity inquiries in prefectures and counties passed through; on their return Zhonghui and others memorialized findings—an edict advanced Yutian magistrate Li Fang one rank, promoted Shunzhou legal officer and acting Yun magistrate Wang Zongyong to Yun sheriff, and dismissed Shunzhou usher Zhang Lin and Yun sheriff Shimowu Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict ordered Zhonghui and Outer Vice Director of the Left Office Pucha Pusuyue to conduct integrity inquiries in the prefectures and counties they visited. On their return Zhonghui and his colleagues reported their findings. An edict advanced Yutian magistrate Li Fang one rank, promoted Shunzhou legal officer and acting Yun magistrate Wang Zongyong to Yun sheriff, and dismissed Shunzhou usher Zhang Lin and Yun sheriff Shimowu Zhe.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複太子右諭德，遷翰林直學士、改棣州防禦使。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother, was recalled from mourning as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, transferred to Direct Academician of the Hanlin, and changed to military commissioner of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was recalled from mourning as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Direct Academician of the Hanlin, and appointed military commissioner of Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 厭次縣捕得強盜數十人，詣州欲以全獲希賞。

translations.literal: Yanci county captured several dozen bandits and brought them to the prefecture hoping reward for a full capture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanci County captured several dozen bandits and brought them to the prefecture hoping to win a reward for a full capture.

sentences.zh: 仲誨疑其有冤，緩其獄。

translations.literal: Zhonghui suspected injustice and slowed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui suspected injustice and slowed the proceedings.

sentences.zh: 同僚曰：「縣境多盜，請置之法，以懲其餘。

translations.literal: Colleagues said: "The county has many bandits; please apply the law to punish the rest.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues said: "The county has many bandits. Please apply the law to deter the rest.

sentences.zh: 」仲誨乃擇老稚者先釋之。

translations.literal: Zhonghui then selected the old and young to release first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui then selected the elderly and children to release first.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乃獲真盜。

translations.literal: Before long the real bandits were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the real bandits were captured.

sentences.zh: 入為禮部侍郎兼左諭德，遷太子詹事兼左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「東宮官屬，尤當選用正人，如行檢不修及不稱位者，具以名聞。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Eastern Palace staff should especially employ upright men; those whose conduct is unrestrained or unfit for office—report their names in full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Eastern Palace staff should especially be upright men. Report by name anyone whose conduct is unrestrained or who is unfit for his post.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「東宮講書或論議間，當以孝儉德行正身之事告之。

translations.literal: He also said: "When lecturing or debating in the Eastern Palace, you should instruct him in filial piety, frugality, virtue, and self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When lecturing or debating in the Eastern Palace, instruct him in filial piety, frugality, virtue, and self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，東宮請增牧人及張設什用，上謂仲誨曰：「太子生於富貴，每教之恭儉。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Eastern Palace requested more herdsmen and expanded furnishings; the emperor told Zhonghui: "The crown prince was born to wealth and rank; I always teach him respect and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the Eastern Palace requested more herdsmen and expanded furnishings. The emperor told Zhonghui: "The crown prince was born to wealth and rank. I always teach him respect and frugality.

sentences.zh: 朕服禦未嘗妄有增益，卿以此意諭之。

translations.literal: I have never rashly added to my wardrobe; convey this meaning to him.
translations.idiomatic: I have never rashly added to my wardrobe. Convey that meaning to him.

sentences.zh: 」改御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，為宋國歲元使，宋主欲變親起接書之儀，遣館伴王抃來議，曲辨強說，欲要以必從。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was Song New Year envoy; the Song ruler wished to change the ritual of rising in person to receive the letter, and sent hostel companion Wang Bian to negotiate, arguing tortuously and insisting he must comply.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he served as the Song New Year envoy. The Song ruler wished to change the ritual of rising in person to receive the letter and sent hostel companion Wang Bian to negotiate, arguing insistently that the Jin side must comply.

sentences.zh: 仲誨曰：「使臣奉命，遠來修好，固欲成禮，而信約所載，非使臣輒敢變更。

translations.literal: Zhonghui said: "The envoy received orders and came from afar to renew friendship; I indeed wish to complete the ritual, but what the covenant records is not something an envoy may rashly alter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui said: "I received orders and came from afar to renew friendship. I certainly wish to complete the ritual, but what the covenant records is not something an envoy may alter on his own.

sentences.zh: 公等宋國腹心，毋僥倖一時，失大國歡。

translations.literal: You are the heart of Song—do not gamble for a moment and lose the great state's goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: You are the heart of Song. Do not gamble for a moment and lose the great state's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 」往復再三，竟用舊儀，親起接書成禮而還。

translations.literal: After repeated exchanges they ultimately used the old ritual; the ruler rose in person to receive the letter, the ceremony was completed, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated exchanges they ultimately used the old ritual. The Song ruler rose in person to receive the letter, the ceremony was completed, and Zhonghui returned.

sentences.zh: 複為太子詹事，遷吏部尚書，轉太子少師兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He again became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and then Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 坐失糾舉大長公主事，與侍御史李瑜各削一階。

translations.literal: For failing to impeach the Grand Princess, he and Attending Censor Li Yu each had one rank stripped.
translations.idiomatic: For failing to impeach the Grand Princess, he and Attending Censor Li Yu each had one rank stripped.

sentences.zh: 仲誨前後為東宮官且十五年，多進規戒，顯宗特加禮敬。

translations.literal: Zhonghui served as Eastern Palace officer for some fifteen years in all, often offering admonitions; Xianzong showed him special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui served as an Eastern Palace officer for roughly fifteen years in all and often offered admonitions. Xianzong showed him special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 仲誨立朝峻整，容色莊重，世宗嘗曰：「朕見劉仲誨嘗若將切諫者。

translations.literal: Zhonghui was stern and orderly at court, his bearing grave; Shizong once said: "When I see Liu Zhonghui it is as if he is about to offer sharp remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghui was stern and orderly at court with a grave bearing. Shizong once said: "Whenever I see Liu Zhonghui it is as if he is about to offer sharp remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 」其以剛嚴見知如此。

translations.literal: Thus he was known for stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: This was how he was known for stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 頍字元矩。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Yuanju.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Yuanju.

sentences.zh: 以大臣子孫充閣門祗候，調莘縣令，召為承奉班都知，遷西上閣門副使兼宮苑令，累遷西上、東上閣門使。

translations.literal: As a minister's descendant he served as usher of the Inner Gate, was assigned magistrate of Xin county, summoned as director of the Presentation Class, transferred to Deputy Usher of the Western Upper Inner Gate and concurrently director of the Palace Parks, and rose through Western and Eastern Upper Inner Gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: As a minister's descendant he served as usher of the Inner Gate, was assigned magistrate of Xin County, summoned as director of the Presentation Class, promoted to Deputy Usher of the Western Upper Inner Gate and director of the Palace Parks, and eventually rose to usher of the Western and Eastern Upper Inner Gates.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，宋盱眙軍報：明年賀正旦使魯 <宜宜>、楊明輝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe the Song Xuyi army reported: next year's New Year congratulatory envoys Lu Yiyi and Yang Minghui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe the Song Xuyi command reported that the next year's New Year envoys would be Lu Yiyi and Yang Minghui.

sentences.zh: 及過界，副使乃王處久。

translations.literal: When they crossed the border, the vice envoy was Wang Chujiu.
translations.idiomatic: When they crossed the border, the vice envoy turned out to be Wang Chujiu.

sentences.zh: 入見，魯<宜宜>殿上不雙跪。

translations.literal: On entering audience Lu Yiyi did not double-kneel in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience Lu Yiyi did not perform the double kneel in the hall.

sentences.zh: 詔<宜宜>就閣詰問先報名銜楊明輝不復報改王處久之故，及不雙跪者。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Yiyi to the pavilion to question him on why the earlier report named Yang Minghui but was not updated when it changed to Wang Chujiu, and on the failure to double-kneel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Yiyi to the pavilion to question him about why the earlier report named Yang Minghui but was not updated when Wang Chujiu replaced him, and about his failure to double-kneel.

sentences.zh: 魯<宜宜>對，拜時並雙跪，有足疾似單跪者。

translations.literal: Lu Yiyi replied that when bowing he double-kneeled both times; a foot ailment made it look like a single kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yiyi replied that he double-kneeled on both bows, but a foot ailment made it appear to be a single kneel.

sentences.zh: 初，南苑有唐舊碑，書「貞元十年御史大夫劉怦葬」。

translations.literal: Earlier in the Southern Park there was an old Tang stele inscribed: "Burial of Censor-in-chief Liu Zheng, tenth year of Zhenyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in the Southern Park there was an old Tang stele reading: "Burial of Censor-in-chief Liu Zheng, tenth year of Zhenyuan."

sentences.zh: 上見之曰：「苑中不宜有墓。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it and said: "A park should not contain a tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw it and said: "A park should not contain a tomb.

sentences.zh: 」頍家本怦後，詔賜頍錢三百貫改葬之。

translations.literal: Yi's family were descendants of Zheng; an edict granted Yi three hundred strings of cash to reinter the remains.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's family were descendants of Zheng. An edict granted Yi three hundred strings of cash to reinter the remains.

sentences.zh: 三遷右宣徽使。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，轉左宣徽使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，致仕，遷一官。

translations.literal: The next year he retired and was advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired and was advanced one rank.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿舊人也，今朝廷多故，豈宜去位。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are an old acquaintance; the court now has many troubles—how can you leave office?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are an old acquaintance. The court now faces many troubles. How can you leave office?

sentences.zh: 朕自東宮薨後，思慮不周，俟稍寧息，即以上郡處卿。

translations.literal: Since the Eastern Palace mourning my thoughts have been unsettled; when things calm a little I shall place you in an upper prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Eastern Palace mourning my thoughts have been unsettled. When things calm a little I shall place you in an upper prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，起為知開封府。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was recalled as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 四年正月元日，攝左宣徽使。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the first month of the fourth year he acted as Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the first month of the fourth year he acted as Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再請老，未半歲複起為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He again requested retirement; within half a year he was recalled as Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested retirement, but within half a year he was recalled as Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 詔安撫河南路，捕盜賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to pacify the Henan Route and capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to pacify the Henan Route and capture bandits.

sentences.zh: 坐與保靜軍節度使會飲，解職。

translations.literal: For drinking with the military commissioner of the Baojing Army he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for drinking with the military commissioner of the Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 起為太子詹事，遷太子少師。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 詹事院欲辟廣東宮周牆，頍請于皇太子曰：「師旅饑饉之際，何為興此役。

translations.literal: The Mentor's Office wished to expand the Eastern Palace perimeter wall; Yi petitioned the crown prince: "In a time of armies and famine, why undertake this project?
translations.idiomatic: The Mentor's Office wished to expand the Eastern Palace perimeter wall. Yi petitioned the crown prince: "In a time of armies and famine, why undertake this project?

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: The project was therefore halted.
translations.idiomatic: The project was therefore halted.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 時立愛

translations.literal: Shi Liai
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liai

sentences.zh: 時立愛，字昌壽，涿州新城人。

translations.literal: Shi Liai, courtesy name Changshou, was a native of Xincheng in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liai, whose courtesy name was Changshou, came from Xincheng in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 父承謙，以財雄鄉里，歲饑發倉廩賑貧乏，假貸者與之折券。

translations.literal: His father Chengqian was wealthy in the district; in years of famine he opened granaries to relieve the poor and tore up the notes of borrowers.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengqian was wealthy in the district. In years of famine he opened his granaries to relieve the poor and tore up the notes of those who owed him.

sentences.zh: 遼太康九年，中進士第，調泰州幕官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang of Liao he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned staff officer in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Liao Taikang he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as a staff officer in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，調同知春州事。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; when mourning ended he was assigned associate prefect of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was assigned associate prefect of Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，遷雲內縣令，再除文德令。

translations.literal: Within a year he was transferred to magistrate of Yunnei, then again appointed magistrate of Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was transferred to magistrate of Yunnei and then appointed magistrate of Wende.

sentences.zh: 樞密院選為吏房副都承旨，轉都承旨。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs selected him as deputy overall usher of the Personnel Section, then overall usher.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs selected him as deputy overall usher of the Personnel Section and then overall usher.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中丞，剛正敢言，忤權貴。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Censor-in-chief, upright and outspoken, offending the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Censor-in-chief, upright and outspoken, and offended the powerful.

sentences.zh: 除燕京副留守，丁母憂，起復舊職，遷遼興軍節度使兼漢軍都統。

translations.literal: He was appointed deputy defender of Yanjing; he mourned his mother, was recalled from mourning to his old post, and was transferred to military commissioner of the Liaoxing Army and concurrently overall commander of the Han armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed deputy defender of Yanjing. After mourning his mother he was recalled from mourning to his old post and was appointed military commissioner of the Liaoxing Army and overall commander of the Han armies.

sentences.zh: 太祖已定燕京，訪求得平州人韓詢持詔招諭平州。

translations.literal: After the Grand Ancestor had secured Yanjing, he sought and found Han Xun of Pingzhou to bear an edict summoning Pingzhou to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Ancestor secured Yanjing, he found Han Xun of Pingzhou and sent him with an edict to summon Pingzhou to submit.

sentences.zh: 是時，奚王回離保在盧能嶺，立愛未敢即朝見，先使人來送款曰：「民情愚執，不即順從，願降寬恩，以慰反側。

translations.literal: At that time the Xi king Huilibao was at Luneng Ridge; Liai did not dare present himself at once but first sent men to offer allegiance, saying: "The people are stubborn and foolish and do not immediately submit; we beg lenient grace to reassure the wavering.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xi king Huilibao was at Luneng Ridge. Liai did not dare present himself at once but first sent men to offer allegiance, saying: "The people are stubborn and do not immediately submit. We beg lenient grace to reassure the wavering.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「朕親巡西土，底定全燕，號令所加，城邑皆下。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I personally toured the western lands and settled all Yan; wherever orders reached, cities submitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "I personally toured the western lands and settled all Yan. Wherever my orders reached, cities submitted.

sentences.zh: 爰嘉忠款，特示優恩，應在彼大小官員可皆充舊職，諸囚禁配隸並從釋免。

translations.literal: I therefore commend your loyalty and show special favor: all officials there great and small may hold their former posts, and all prisoners and assigned servants are released.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore commend your loyalty and show special favor. All officials there, great and small, may hold their former posts, and all prisoners and assigned servants are released.

sentences.zh: 」於是，遼帝尚在天德，平州雖降，民心未固。

translations.literal: At this time the Liao emperor was still at Tiande; though Pingzhou had submitted, popular sentiment was not yet firm.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Liao emperor was still at Tiande. Although Pingzhou had submitted, popular sentiment was not yet firm.

sentences.zh: 奚王回離保軍所在保聚，薊州已降複叛。

translations.literal: Where the Xi king Huilibao's army gathered they held together; Jizhou had submitted but rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Xi king Huilibao's army gathered the people held together. Jizhou had submitted but rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 民間流言謂：「金人所下城邑，始則存撫，後則俘掠。

translations.literal: Popular rumor said: "In cities taken by the Jin people, at first they console and cherish, afterward they capture and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Popular rumor said: "In cities taken by the Jin, at first they console the people, but afterward they capture and plunder them.

sentences.zh: 」時立愛雖開諭而不肯信，乃上表：「乞下明詔，遣官分行郡邑，宣諭德義。

translations.literal: Though Liai instructed them they would not believe, and he memorialized: "We beg a clear edict sending officials through the prefectures and counties to proclaim virtue and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liai instructed them they would not believe. He memorialized: "We beg a clear edict sending officials through the prefectures and counties to proclaim virtue and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 他日兵臨于宋，順則撫之，逆則討之，兵不勞而天下定矣。

translations.literal: When troops later reach Song, if they submit then console them, if they resist then punish them—the realm will be settled without weary armies.
translations.idiomatic: When troops later reach Song, if they submit then console them, if they resist then punish them. The realm will be settled without weary armies.

sentences.zh: 」上覽表嘉之，詔答曰：「卿始率吏民歸附，複條利害，悉合朕意，嘉歎不忘。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial with approval and replied by edict: "You first led officials and people to submit, then set out advantages and harms—all accord with my intent; my praise does not fade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with approval and replied by edict: "You first led officials and people to submit, then set out advantages and harms. All of this accords with my intent, and my praise does not fade.

sentences.zh: 山西部族緣遼主未獲，恐陰相連結，故遷處於嶺東。

translations.literal: Tribal groups of Shanxi, because the Liao ruler was not yet captured, might secretly link together; therefore they were moved east of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal groups of Shanxi, because the Liao ruler had not yet been captured, might secretly link together, so they were moved east of the passes.

sentences.zh: 西京人民既無異望，皆按堵如故。

translations.literal: The people of the Western Capital had no disloyal intent and all remained settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Western Capital had no disloyal intent and all remained settled as before.

sentences.zh: 或有將卒貪悍，冒犯紀律，輒掠降人者。

translations.literal: Some officers and soldiers were greedy and fierce, violated discipline, and plundered those who had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Some officers and soldiers were greedy and fierce, violated discipline, and plundered those who had submitted.

sentences.zh: 已諭諸部及軍帥，約束兵士，秋毫有犯，必刑無赦。

translations.literal: I have instructed all divisions and army commanders to restrain the troops; the slightest offense will be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: I have instructed all divisions and army commanders to restrain the troops. The slightest offense will be punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 今遣斡羅阿裏等為卿副貳，以撫斯民，其告諭所部，使知朕意。」

translations.literal: Now I send Woluo Ali and others as your deputies to console this people; proclaim to your jurisdiction so they know my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Now I send Woluo Ali and others as your deputies to console this people. Proclaim to your jurisdiction so they know my intent."

sentences.zh: 其後，以平州為南京，用張覺為留守，時立愛遂去平州。

translations.literal: Afterward Pingzhou was made the Southern Capital and Zhang Jue was used as defender; Liai then left Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Pingzhou was made the Southern Capital with Zhang Jue as defender, and Liai then left Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 而張覺遂因燕京人東徙，其眾怨望，覺遂叛入于宋。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue then, because people of Yanjing were moved east, found his followers resentful, and rebelled and fled to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue then found his followers resentful because people of Yanjing were moved east, and he rebelled and fled to Song.

sentences.zh: 立愛既去平州歸鄉里，太祖以燕、薊與宋，新城入于宋。

translations.literal: After Liai left Pingzhou and returned home, the Grand Ancestor ceded Yan and Ji to Song, and Xincheng came under Song.
translations.idiomatic: After Liai left Pingzhou and returned home, the Grand Ancestor ceded Yan and Ji to Song, and Xincheng came under Song.

sentences.zh: 宋累詔立愛，立愛見宋政日壞，不肯起，戒其宗族不得求仕。

translations.literal: Song repeatedly summoned Liai; seeing Song government daily worsen, he would not take office and warned his clan not to seek posts.
translations.idiomatic: Song repeatedly summoned Liai, but seeing Song government grow worse by the day, he refused to take office and warned his clan not to seek posts.

sentences.zh: 韓企先

translations.literal: Han Qixian
translations.idiomatic: Han Qixian

sentences.zh: 初，太祖定燕京，始用漢官宰相賞左企弓等，置中書省、樞密院于廣寧府，而朝廷宰相自用女直官號。

translations.literal: At first, when the Grand Ancestor secured Yanjing, he began using Han officials as chancellors such as Zuo Qigong, establishing the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs at Guangning prefecture, while court chancellors still used Jurchen titles.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor first secured Yanjing, he began appointing Han officials such as Zuo Qigong as chancellors and established the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs at Guangning, while court chancellors still used Jurchen titles.

sentences.zh: 太宗初年，無所改更。

translations.literal: Early in Taizong's reign nothing was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizong's reign nothing was changed.

sentences.zh: 及張敦固伏誅，移置中書、樞密于平州，蔡靖以燕山降，移置燕京，凡漢地選授調發租稅皆承制行之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dungu was executed, the Secretariat and Bureau were moved to Pingzhou; when Cai Jing surrendered the Yan Mountains they were moved to Yanjing—all appointments, levies, and taxes in Han territory were carried out by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dungu was executed, the Secretariat and Bureau were moved to Pingzhou. When Cai Jing surrendered the Yan Mountains they were moved to Yanjing. All appointments, levies, and taxes in Han territory were carried out by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 故自時立愛、劉彥宗及企先輩，官為宰相，其職大抵如此。

translations.literal: Therefore from Shi Liai, Liu Yanzong, and Qixian's generation onward, though titled chancellor, their duties were broadly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from the time of Shi Liai, Liu Yanzong, and Qixian onward, though titled chancellor, their duties were broadly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 斜也、宗幹當國，勸太宗改女直舊制，用漢官制度。

translations.literal: When Xieye and Zonggan held power they urged Taizong to change the old Jurchen system and use Han official institutions.
translations.idiomatic: When Xieye and Zonggan held power they urged Taizong to change the old Jurchen system and adopt Han official institutions.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，始定官制，立尚書省以下諸司府寺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui the official system was first fixed, establishing the Department of State Affairs and the bureaus, offices, and courts below it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhui the official system was first fixed, establishing the Department of State Affairs and the bureaus, offices, and courts beneath it.

sentences.zh: 十年，司空李德固孫引慶求襲其祖猛安，世宗曰：「德固無功，其猛安且闕之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Grand Preceptor Li Degu's grandson Yinqing sought to inherit his grandfather's meng'an; Shizong said: "Degu had no merit—let his meng'an remain vacant for now.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Grand Preceptor Li Degu's grandson Yinqing sought to inherit his grandfather's meng'an. Shizong said: "Degu had no merit. Let his meng'an remain vacant for now.

sentences.zh: 漢人宰相惟韓企先最賢，他不及也。

translations.literal: Among Han chancellors only Han Qixian was most worthy; none else matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han chancellors only Han Qixian was most worthy. None else matched him.

sentences.zh: 」十一年，將圖功臣像于衍慶宮，上曰：「丞相企先，本朝典章制度多出斯人之手，至於關決大政，與大臣謀議，不使外人知之，由是無人能知其功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when planning portraits of meritorious officials in the Yansqing Palace, the emperor said: "Chancellor Qixian—most of this dynasty's statutes and institutions came from this man's hand; as for deciding great affairs and deliberating with ministers, he did not let outsiders know, so no one could know his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when planning portraits of meritorious officials in the Yansqing Palace, the emperor said: "Chancellor Qixian produced most of this dynasty's statutes and institutions. In deciding great affairs and deliberating with ministers he did not let outsiders know, so no one could fully know his merit.

sentences.zh: 前後漢人宰相無能及者，置功臣畫像中，亦足以示勸後人。

translations.literal: No Han chancellor before or after could match him; placing him among the painted meritorious officials is enough to admonish later generations.
translations.idiomatic: No Han chancellor before or after could match him. Placing him among the painted meritorious officials is enough to admonish later generations.

sentences.zh: 」十五年，諡簡懿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was given the posthumous name Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was given the posthumous name Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 子 鐸

translations.literal: Son Duo
translations.idiomatic: Son Duo

sentences.zh: 韓鐸字振文，企先次子也。

translations.literal: Han Duo, courtesy name Zhenwen, was Qixian's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Han Duo, whose courtesy name was Zhenwen, was Qixian's second son.

sentences.zh: 皇統末，以大臣子授武義將軍。

translations.literal: Near the end of Huangtong, as a minister's son he was appointed General of Martial Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Huangtong, as a minister's son he was appointed General of Martial Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 熙宗聞其有儒學，賜進士第，除宣徽判官。

translations.literal: Xizong heard he had Confucian learning, granted him the jinshi degree, and appointed him adjutant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong heard he had Confucian learning, granted him the jinshi degree, and appointed him adjutant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑部員外郎，海陵遣中使諭之曰：「郎官，高選也。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Outer Director of the Ministry of Justice; Hailing sent a palace envoy to instruct him: "A bureau director is a high selection.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Outer Director of the Ministry of Justice. Hailing sent a palace envoy to instruct him: "A bureau director is a high selection.

sentences.zh: 汝勳賢之子，行已蒞官，能世其家，故以命汝。

translations.literal: You are the son of a meritorious worthy; your conduct in taking office can continue your house—therefore you are appointed.
translations.idiomatic: You are the son of a meritorious worthy. Your conduct in taking office can continue your house, and therefore you are appointed.

sentences.zh: 苟能夙夜在公，當不次擢用，雖公相可到。

translations.literal: If you can labor day and night in public service, you will be promoted out of turn—even chancellor is reachable.
translations.idiomatic: If you labor day and night in public service, you will be promoted out of turn. Even the chancellorship is within reach.

sentences.zh: 」鐸感奮，獄或有疑，據經議讞。

translations.literal: Duo was stirred and inspired; when cases were doubtful he judged punishments by the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was stirred and inspired. When cases were doubtful he judged punishments according to the classics.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，改兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song he was changed to Outer Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing campaigned against Song he was appointed Outer Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 大定初，遷本部郎中，累官河州防禦使，求養親，解去。

translations.literal: Early in Dading he was transferred to Director of his ministry, rose through offices to military commissioner of Hezhou, requested to care for his parents, and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he was promoted to Director of his ministry, eventually rose to military commissioner of Hezhou, requested leave to care for his parents, and resigned.

sentences.zh: 召為左諫議大夫，遷中都路都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Remonstrating Grand Master and transferred to overall transport commissioner of the Zhongdu Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Left Remonstrating Grand Master and appointed overall transport commissioner of the Zhongdu Route.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上謂宰臣曰：「韓鐸年高，不任繁劇，且其母老矣，可與之便郡。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the emperor told the chancellors: "Han Duo is advanced in years and cannot bear heavy duties; moreover his mother is old—give him a convenient prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the emperor told the chancellors: "Han Duo is advanced in years and cannot bear heavy duties. Moreover his mother is old. Give him a convenient prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」於是改順天軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was therefore changed to military commissioner of the Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore appointed military commissioner of the Shuntian Army.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：太祖入燕，始用遼南、北面官僚制度。

translations.literal: Appreciation: When the Grand Ancestor entered Yan he first used the Liao southern and northern-face bureaucratic systems.
translations.idiomatic: Appreciation: When the Grand Ancestor entered Yan he first used the Liao southern and northern bureaucratic systems.

sentences.zh: 是故劉彥宗、時立愛規為施設，不見於朝廷之上。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Yanzong and Shi Liai planned and established arrangements not visible at the central court.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Liu Yanzong and Shi Liai planned and established arrangements that were not visible at the central court.

sentences.zh: 軍旅之暇，治官政，庀民事，務農積穀，內供京師，外給轉餉，此其功也。

translations.literal: In intervals between campaigns they governed official affairs, arranged civil matters, urged farming and stored grain, supplied the capital within and transport provisions without—this was their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals between campaigns they governed official affairs, arranged civil matters, urged farming and stored grain, supplied the capital within and transport provisions without. This was their achievement.

sentences.zh: 韓企先入相兩朝，幾二十年，成功著業，世宗稱其賢焉。

translations.literal: Han Qixian entered the chancellorship under two reigns for nearly twenty years, achieved success and left a lasting record, and Shizong praised his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qixian served as chancellor under two reigns for nearly twenty years, achieved lasting success, and Shizong praised his worth.
